To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fixed point of a graph neural network can be computed by finding saddle points of the corresponding Lagrangian function.

the fixed point computation in Graph Neural Networks can be recast as a constrained optimization procedure, and the resulting method is able to achieve state of the art results on multiple standard benchmarks.

1) We cast the fixed point iteration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) as a saddle point optimization problem, thus allowing for a better understanding of the underlying dynamics; 2) We propose a new GNN architecture, based on the proposed optimization formulation, which is more efficient, and achieves better results on multiple standard benchmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) the theoretical foundation of the Lagrangization approach to GNNs; (2) the practical implementation of the Lagrangians for GNNs; and (3) the experimental evaluation of the Lagrangizations on standard benchmarks for GNNs.

, in the context of GNNs, Lagrangian methods provide a general and effective framework to design new architectures, which can be used to address a variety of problems, including the design of novel loss functions and the definition of new inductive biases.
